strategy.thesis: Company builder / startup holding company: spots a large market opportunity, then directly ideates, staffs, funds and operates new companies in-house rather than passively investing. Widely cited as Korea's first company builder.

application.how_to_apply: Company builder; ventures are built in-house rather than via open application. Investment activity via Fast Ventures subsidiary.

summary.en: Founded in 2012 by the TicketMonster founders, Fast Track Asia is widely cited as South Korea's first company builder. Rather than investing passively, it ideates, staffs and operates ventures in-house. Park Ji-woong has launched 11 companies over 11 years; current operating arms include FastFive (co-working), Day One Company (adult education), Fast Ventures (VC) and Fast Investment (PE). Exits include HelloNature (to SK Planet) and FoodFly (to Delivery Hero). Krafton invested ₩22.3B for a 27.47% stake to become the largest shareholder.

summary.en: Founded in 2013 by KAIST PhD Ryu Joong-hee, FuturePlay is a deep-tech company builder that combines incubation, acceleration and VC. Its TechUP program co-founds companies with technical engineers, and TechUP+ partners with large corporates. As of 2024 it managed ₩276.8B AUM across multiple funds, with 252 cumulative portfolio companies; notable exits to IPO include Innospace and SOS Lab.

summary.en: The Korean arm of global venture builder Antler, launched in Seoul in 2021 and led by serial entrepreneur Jiho Kang (Soomgo co-founder). Its 'Startup Generator' residency brings individual founders together to form teams and validate ideas over an ~11-week residency (6-month cycle, twice a year), then invests $110K (₩150M) at pre-seed with a follow-on commitment of $150K–$370K. Antler Korea has made ~101 investments.

summary.en: &Beyond is a company builder founded in 2013 by Park Chul-joon, a former Bain & Company consultant. It pairs M&A and business-planning expertise to create new ventures, historically with an offline-business focus. Its first venture was U Moment (operating 'The Chapel' wedding hall in Cheongdam-dong, 2014); it also built AI company Skelter Labs, which was acquired by Metanet in 2024.

strategy.thesis: Hardware-focused accelerator / maker studio that helps hardware founders build products: provides initial investment plus prototype production, a domestic/overseas factory network, and mass-production linkage. Described as Korea's only dedicated hardware accelerator.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via n15.asia / its program calls.

summary.en: Founded in 2015 in Yongsan's Najin Electronics Arcade, N15 (Enfifteen) is Korea's dedicated hardware accelerator and maker studio. It backs hardware founders with initial investment plus hands-on prototype and mass-production support via a domestic/overseas factory network; it has helped produce products for 96+ startups and serves as a government early-startup-package operator. Co-founded by Huh Je and Ryu Sun-jong.

summary.en: Grande Clip is a company builder founded by Kim Bong-jin, founder of food-delivery unicorn Baemin (Woowa Brothers). It creates consumer-brand ventures from creative concepts — e.g. New Mix Coffee, the paper-toy brand What a Wonder, and Magazine C — and expands by acquisition, taking a 50% stake in accommodation platform Stayfolio in July 2024.

summary.en: Bluepoint Partners is a Daejeon-based deep-tech accelerator founded in 2014 by KAIST physics PhD Lee Yong-kwan (who sold Plasmart to NASDAQ-listed MKS). Beyond acceleration it has moved into company building: in 2022 it launched its first company-building project, the children's-space subsidiary Differentdoors, backed by a dedicated Portfolio Growth Team. It is among Korea's first accelerators to pursue an IPO.
